messages:
maria: Hey team — I opened a PR to add a "data disposition" subsection to the security docs. Need quick checks on SOC 2-friendly wording, retention phrasing, and a tiny SDK snippet for sanitized audit exports. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4820 :eyes:

raj: Thanks — linking. My main ask: we should be explicit about 'redact PII at export' and give an example config. Keep retention language flexible (default 365 days) but show how to configure.

becca: Legal quick note: say "SOC 2" (two words) in copy, call out customer-configurable retention and lawful deletion requests. Avoid promising deletion from third-party mirrors.

leo: I can add an example of server-side redaction middleware. Short snippet below — pls verify style for docs.

leo: ```js
// server-side audit export redaction example
const exportConfig = {
  retention_days: 365,
  redact_fields: ["user_email","credit_card","ssn"],
  keep_fields: ["event_type","resource_id","timestamp","actor_id"]
};

function sanitizeEvent(e, cfg) {
  const copy = {...e};
  cfg.redact_fields.forEach(f => { if (copy[f]) copy[f] = "<REDACTED>" });
  return copy;
}
```

sasha: This looks good. Two small suggestions: use `retention_days` as an optional override and show how to set a default via the console or SDK. And add a sentence on KMS-backed key rotation for stored logs.

maria: Good call. I'll add a one-line note on KMS/HSM and link to the key management page. Also adding `console default` example.

maria: Proposed doc wording (short): "Audit records are retained by default for 365 days. Customers may configure retention periods per-tenant; exports can be sanitized to redact PII fields before download. For regulated deletion requests, Redwood removes content from managed stores, but customers are responsible for any downstream copies or backups."

raj: Suggest tweak: change "removes content from managed stores" -> "purges content from Redwood-managed storage within retention constraints and deletion policies" — slightly more precise.

becca: +1 to raj's phrasing. Also add a short bullet: "We do not promise deletion from external backups or mirrors" so legal is clear.

maria: Updated in PR text. Also added a tiny SDK snippet for doing a sanitized export client-side. Pls check:```python
# client-side example to request sanitized audit export
from redwood import AuditClient
client = AuditClient(api_key=ENV["REDWOOD_KEY"])
resp = client.export_logs(
  start="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  end="2025-02-01T00:00:00Z",
  sanitize={"redact": ["user_email","ip_address"]},
  retention_days_override=None
)
print(resp.download_url)
```

leo: Tiny nit: use `sanitize={"redact_fields": [...]}` to match server-sample naming. Also show how to request a CSV vs JSON.

maria: Done. I also fixed the doc link target and the anchor IDs that were broken. Edge case question: should we include a short example policy for data-subject requests (GDPR) or just link to privacy?

becca: Link to privacy + add one sentence: "For data subject requests, follow your account admin flow; Redwood will assist with exports and purges from managed storage."

docs-bot: Reminder: please add the PR label `docs/security` and link the updated snippet to the code-samples page.

infra-bot: Deploy preview for PR 4820 available at https://deploy-preview.docs.redwood.ai/4820 (build passed)

maria: Great — I'll merge after one more 👍 from security and legal. Thanks everyone! :rocket:
